findings: Thin pale, intermittently dotted edging remains around portions of the machine, cables, clothing and shoes, visible against dark backgrounds. No broad opaque background or substantial interior residue is visible.

The left machine upright/pulley shifts right and the seat support geometry changes in male frame 3 relative to earlier frames, while feet and right upright remain nearly anchored. This is limited equipment jitter, distinct from the intended arm extension.

Thin light outlines/residual edge pixels follow portions of the arms, legs, hair and machine bases/uprights. More apparent on dark backgrounds; limited in extent and does not obscure the illustration.
Thin pale outlines and scattered light edge pixels are visible against the dark background around portions of the athlete and machine. No substantial opaque interior background remains.

Machine base, upright and platform positions drift slightly between frames, particularly female 1 to 2 and male 0 to 3. These fixed parts should remain stationary; shifts are limited and the illustrations remain usable.
Thin pale/jagged fringe traces portions of hair, limbs, clothing and plate edges on dark backgrounds. Illustrations remain usable; no substantial exterior background or checkerboard block is visible.
Male frame 0 plate center contains a bright white fill that remains white on the dark background, unlike a transparent opening. Small localized equipment-interior artifact.
Small bright white remnants remain in the transparent gap beneath the raised head/between the arms, conspicuous on the dark background.
Thin pale edging is visible along portions of the back, hair and mat perimeter on dark backgrounds. Illustrations remain usable; no large opaque background or substantial cutout holes observed.

Small intermittent pale edge pixels/fringes are visible on dark backgrounds around the shoe outlines and some body/hair contours, most noticeable around the female ponytail. These are limited perimeter artifacts; no opaque background or substantial interior residue is visible.

Small opaque pale remnants extend beyond shoe soles (especially setup frames and frame 2), beneath the grounded plates in both setup frames, and along portions of the female ponytail/neck edge in frames 1–3. Most visible against dark background; illustrations remain usable.
A thin, disconnected dashed vertical light line remains near the right canvas edge, clearly visible on the dark background.
Thin pale fringes trace portions of the athlete and equipment contours on dark backgrounds. Artwork remains clearly usable; no opaque background or substantial interior residue is visible.

Male frame 2 shifts the athlete and bar left and the shoe baseline upward relative to the other frames; female frame 0 has visibly larger/wider plates and bar than frame 1 despite a similar setup pose. These are limited animation inconsistencies, distinct from the intended vertical lift.

Small bright white remnants are visible on dark backgrounds: a wedge beneath the left plate in male frame 1, and small flecks along the female ponytail in frames 0–2. These are limited edge artifacts, not a full opaque background.

Stationary wooden blocks shift laterally and vary modestly in size across each sequence, especially female frame 2. This causes limited background-equipment jitter independent of the intended athlete/bar movement.
Thin intermittent pale fringe/specks are visible along inner arm-to-torso cutout boundaries on the dark background. Limited edge residue; no large opaque background or checkerboard interiors.

Small elongated gaps in the metallic bar shaft/sleeves switch from black on the dark composite to light on the light composite, indicating unwanted transparency in solid equipment. The bar remains continuous and recognizable.
Thin pale, slightly speckled fringe follows portions of the hair, clothing and limb contours on the dark background; limited to the cutout edge and does not obscure the illustration.

Thin pale broken fringe outlines portions of the rack, plates, bench and athlete on dark backgrounds; especially visible around female ponytails. Limited to edges, with no substantial opaque background or enclosed checkerboard visible.

Bench/rack uprights, base feet and planted shoes shift modestly horizontally between frames. These stationary anchor changes are separate from the intended bar and arm motion; overall scale and identity remain broadly consistent.

Thin light fringe follows parts of the athlete and bench contours on dark backgrounds. White shoe sole strips show irregular transparent breaks, most conspicuous in male frame 0, which also has small pale flecks beneath the soles. Illustration remains usable; no substantial background block or enclosed checkerboard is visible.

Female frame 0 places bench and feet slightly lower than subsequent frames; bench legs and foot positions vary slightly through the sequence. This is limited stationary-anchor drift rather than the intended arm press motion.

The male bar changes apparent width and bend geometry across the curl, and its band connections change from wrapped loops in frame 0 to carabiner-like fittings in frames 1–3. Equipment remains recognizable and connected, but this produces a small continuity mismatch.
Male frame 3 and female frame 2 introduce visibly denser speckled clothing texture than the neighboring frames, causing a small shading/style discontinuity.

Foot outlines and stance width shift slightly across otherwise stationary standing poses, most evident in male frame 3 and female frames 1–3. Overall figure scale is similar and no severe jump or clipping is visible.

Small opaque white wedges remain in the gap between the image-right arm and torso; frames 1 and 3 also show white in the opposite bent-arm gap. These remain white against the dark background. Localized remnants do not obscure the movement.

Thin pale fringe and scattered tiny edge flecks are visible around silhouettes on dark backgrounds, especially shoes and portions of head/limb contours. Female shoe edges have the clearest small stray marks. No large background field or clipping.
Thin pale outlines trace portions of the body, handles and bands against dark backgrounds. Artwork remains usable; no substantial exterior background remains.

The small opaque pale ground oval beneath the feet contains blocky/checker-like tonal patches and stands out on dark backgrounds. Its oval shape appears intentional, but its patterned texture warrants review.

Fine light-gray/white contour residue is visible against black along portions of the body, shoes, hair, and enclosed gaps. It is narrow and does not obscure anatomy or materially compromise the illustration. Light-background presentation is substantially cleaner.

Thin pale, intermittently dotted fringe follows portions of the cutout contours on dark backgrounds, especially hair, arms, shoes and ground ellipses. Light-background rendering is largely clean; no substantial opaque background or checkerboard interiors observed.

Male ground ellipse and planted shoe rise modestly through frames 1 and 2, then return lower in frame 3. This creates a limited ground-anchor shift beyond the expected torso lowering during the lunge.

Thin pale, intermittently dotted fringe traces portions of the hair, arms, torso, legs and equipment on dark backgrounds. Limited to the perimeter; illustrations remain usable. No large opaque background, enclosed checkerboard residue, substantial unwanted holes or clipping seen.
Enclosed sole bands and lace details switch from light to dark with the preview background, indicating cut-out footwear interiors. The affected areas are small and the illustrations remain usable.
A thin gray/brown strip follows the underside of the shorts and torso, visible on the dark background. It is limited perimeter residue rather than a large opaque background.
Male frame 2 exposes a broad skin-colored band around the abdominal highlight while frames 0, 1 and 3 show a full shirt with the highlight over it. This produces a visible clothing continuity change.

Planted shoes shift in position and change shape modestly between frames, especially female 0 to 1; the torso rise is legitimate crunch motion, but the feet do not remain fully anchored. Illustrations remain usable.
Thin pale fringe follows portions of athlete, dumbbell and bench contours on the dark background. Limited to narrow edges; no opaque background blocks or substantial interior residue observed.

The stationary bench shifts modestly between frames: male frames 2 and 3 sit higher than 0 and 1, and female frame 0 sits slightly lower than subsequent frames. Bench feet and supports move along with the body, independently of the intended arm movement. Overall scale remains similar and all artwork stays within the canvas.
Thin pale dotted fringe remains along portions of the athlete and bench contours on dark backgrounds. It is limited to the perimeter; no opaque background or substantial interior residue is visible.

Stationary bench feet and head support shift between male frames, particularly from frame 0 to frames 1/2. This is visible anchor drift beyond the intended arm movement, but the illustration remains usable.

Shoe sole bands and lace details, plus thin strips on the machine base/uprights, take on the comparison background color and disappear on dark backgrounds. These are limited cutouts of apparent material highlights, not opaque white residue. Both circular grip ends also take on the background; whether those ends were intended as open tubes is uncertain and is not the basis for severity. Illustration remains usable.

The stationary seat/backrest geometry changes height and shape across the ordered frames, most visibly in frame 2, while the floor base stays broadly anchored. This introduces limited machine wobble beyond the intended torso and arm movement; no large overall scale jump.
Male frame 3 uses hexagonal dumbbell heads, whereas male frames 0–2 use round plate dumbbells. Equipment remains complete and usable, but its design changes during the sequence.

Small changes in foot spacing, shoe angles and lower-body contours occur between otherwise stationary standing poses, most noticeable from male frame 0 to 1 and female frame 0 to 1. Overall height and floor position stay close; this is limited animation continuity variation rather than a large scale shift.

Thin pale outlining remains around portions of the athletes and equipment. Small irregular light-gray patches extend beyond the soles; frame 2 in both variants also has a pale patch beneath the lowered knee. These are conspicuous on dark backgrounds but limited in area; the artwork remains usable.

Irregular pale gray/white ground patches remain around and between the shoes in every frame. Fine light edge speckles also surround portions of hair, limbs and dumbbells. These are conspicuous against dark backgrounds but limited in area; the figures remain usable.

Pale ragged edging and small residual light patches are visible on the dark background around equipment feet, shoe edges and some athlete contours. Bench support undersides and the left bottom corner of the red box show the clearest residue. No broad opaque background or checkerboard interior is visible.

Across each sequence the bench moves right and the target box moves left, narrowing their spacing despite both being stationary equipment. This is distinct from the athlete's intended forward/upward jump. The drift is noticeable but the movement remains understandable.
Male frame 3 shows a small visible gap between the straight-legged athlete's shoes and the box top, making the final standing/landing pose appear to hover.

Thin pale, irregular fringe and small dashed remnants remain around parts of the cutout, most clearly beneath the bench feet and around shoe soles on the dark background. No opaque exterior field or enclosed checkerboard is visible.

Bench feet, seat and step shift slightly between frames in both sequences; frame 3 also lowers the seated figure relative to earlier frames. These stationary-equipment changes are separate from the intended heel lift, but are limited and leave the exercise readable.

Small irregular pale/white remnants between and beneath shoes and around bench feet, with thin light fringe on portions of the cutout perimeter. Most visible against dark background; limited in area and does not obscure the movement.

Tiny isolated spots on knees (male 1 and 3; female 0 and 2) and face (female 3) change from dark to light with the preview background, consistent with small unintended transparent pinholes. These are limited specks, not substantial anatomy loss.

Irregular pale gray/white patches extend beyond the shoe soles, especially at heels and along the ground edge, visibly separate from the intended sole contour on dark backgrounds. Thin intermittent pale edge speckling also occurs along skin/clothing and female hair contours. These are limited artifacts; figures remain usable.

Irregular pale gray/white residue extends beyond the shoe soles into the surrounding transparent floor area; thin intermittent light fringes also trace parts of the figure/equipment outlines. Visible on dark backgrounds, limited in area, with the illustrations otherwise usable.

Both sequences show limited sideways drift of the planted shoes/lower body, most evident comparing frame 0 with frame 2 and the return frame. This is separate from the intended elbow motion. Scale remains broadly consistent; the shift is small and does not make the exercise unusable.
Small isolated skin-colored sliver near the far left edge, below the extended shoe, disconnected from the athlete. Visible on both backgrounds; the principal figure remains intact.

Small background-colored oval slots at the ponytail attachment in all female frames; additional tiny transparent spots in the bent-leg shoe upper in frames 2 and 3. These appear to remove small interior details, most evident on the light background.

Female frame 0 has plain black shorts, while frames 1–3 show a conspicuous red side seam and split trim. The lower side panel remains visible below the lowered hand in frame 0, so occlusion does not fully explain the missing trim. This causes a small clothing-detail pop in the sequence; the illustration remains usable.

A narrow pale/gray fringe traces portions of the athlete and equipment contours on the dark previews, especially hair, arms and machine edges. It is small and does not obscure the illustration. No substantial enclosed checkerboard or white background residue was observed.

The male sequence has limited horizontal drift of the planted shoes and body between phases, most evident from frame 1 to frame 2. Height and floor level remain broadly consistent; the small lateral shifts are separate from the intended elbow/bar motion and may cause mild animation jitter.

The female sequence has limited horizontal drift of the planted shoes and body between phases, most evident from frame 1 to frame 2. Height and floor level remain broadly consistent; the small lateral shifts are separate from the intended elbow/bar motion and may cause mild animation jitter.

Thin pale, intermittently dashed fringe follows the athlete outline and rope on the dark background. Most evident around hair, shoes and rope loop; illustrations remain usable and light-background display largely conceals it.

Male frame 3 is slightly smaller overall than the preceding frames, with a lower head and shorter torso/figure. The change exceeds the local leg movement but is limited, not a major animation mismatch.
A thin flat gray/tan ground strip remains beneath the massage ball, visible on both backgrounds and absent from the other frames.
Female frame 0 has a cropped top and exposed waist; frames 1–3 show a longer top covering the waist. This creates a visible clothing change during playback.

Supporting hand, torso and bent-leg positions vary modestly between frames, with some changes in body proportions and massage-ball size. These exceed just the intended ankle/foot roll but remain limited; the exercise is readable throughout.

The top ponytail tip is almost flush with the canvas edge, leaving only one pixel of transparent top padding. The contour remains visible, but this is unusually tight framing. No definite clipping is visible.

Thin green edge residue is visible against dark and light backgrounds along portions of hair, skin, clothing, shoes and barbell outlines. Particularly evident throughout the female set; smaller traces appear in male frames 1–3. Illustration interiors remain intact and usable.
Thin pale, broken fringe follows portions of the hair, arms, legs, cable and ground-shadow perimeter in both return frames. It is visible on the dark background; artwork remains intact and usable.

Frame 0 has no continuous oval ground shadow (female frame 0 retains small dark patches at the feet/pulley), while frames 1–3 have an oval shadow joining the feet and pulley. This produces a small background pop at the loop boundary. Foot and pulley positions also drift slightly, without a large scale mismatch.

Thin pale, occasionally dotted fringe follows portions of the outer contours, equipment edges and shoes on the dark background. Limited in extent; no substantial exterior residue or opaque background.

Male frame 1 has visibly flatter leg/knee shading and straighter, forward-facing shoes than the other three frames, with a slightly lower head position. This produces a limited visual pop; identity and exercise remain recognizable.
Female frame 1 has a slightly higher shoe baseline than frames 0, 2 and 3 despite the standing movement, creating modest vertical anchor drift.
Small opaque white wedges remain between the hanging forearm and bench in female frame 0 and between the dumbbells above the lap in female frame 3. They remain white on the dark background.

Fine pale contour fringe is visible on dark backgrounds, with small detached flecks particularly beneath female shoes/bench and around the male frame 3 left shoe. Limited in area; illustrations remain usable.

Bench feet and planted shoes drift across each sequence, most visibly in male frames 2 and 3 compared with 0 and 1. Female bench support/adjustment-knob detail also changes from frame 0 to later frames. These stationary-object changes are separate from the intended arm raise; overall exercise remains recognizable.

White shoe sole/stripe details partially disappear into the dark background while appearing continuous against light, indicating small transparency losses within shoe artwork. Fine pale speckling traces some outlines, especially shoes. The figures remain usable; no substantial clothing holes or opaque checkerboard interiors were seen.

The planted foot and upper body drift modestly rightward from setup to later poses, more noticeably in the female sequence. Height and baseline are otherwise reasonably stable. This is limited anchor inconsistency rather than a large scale jump; some torso shift is natural for balance.
